target_customer: Mac users who wanted hands free control of media apps; no paying customer model was stated
problem: Gesture control needed special hardware like Kinect; Flutter used an ordinary webcam to let users pause and play media with a hand wave.
business_model: Free consumer desktop app (Mac, later Chrome support) with technology value for a larger acquirer

founders.name: Navneet Dalal
founders.background_notes: Co-founded Flutter with Mehul Nariyawala; one search summary said he previously worked at Google but I did not open a source for it, so it is not recorded.

founders.name: Mehul Nariyawala
founders.background_notes: YC page: later product management lead at Nest; co-founder of Matic. Education not listed.

exit.reason: Google said it would support and collaborate on the team's research; terms not disclosed, TechCrunch reported unconfirmed talk of about 40 million dollars.

competitors.name: Microsoft Kinect
competitors.what: Depth camera gesture control requiring special hardware

competitors.name: Existing gesture control software tied to certain devices
competitors.what: Software limited to specific devices or special hardware

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable hand gesture recognition from ordinary webcams under varied lighting is computer vision research; Google later bought the team for its technology.

defensibility.rationale: A computer vision model for webcams was hard to replicate quickly, but the consumer app had no lock in or network effects.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google acquired Flutter in Oct 2013; Intel bought rival Omek around the same time per TechCrunch.

market_need_then: The app reached about 1 million desktop users, topped Mac App Store charts in 14 countries and was downloaded in over 90 countries, showing consumer curiosity, though no revenue or paying need was reported.

branding.domain_note: Used flutterapp.com; the exact .com was not obtained as the app domain.
branding.brand_signature: Waving a hand to pause music
branding.community_and_virality: Ranked top five in the Mac App Store in about 30 countries in its first two weeks per TechCrunch; press from MIT Technology Review and others. The name was later reused by Google's Flutter framework, which is a different product.

brand_strength.rationale: A catchy name and a simple demo that spread via app store charts and tech press, though no brand assets were documented.

outcome_analysis: Flutter raised a 1.4 million dollar seed in Jun 2012 after YC and built a webcam gesture app that reached about 1 million desktop users. Google acquired it in Oct 2013, with a reported but unconfirmed price near 40 million dollars. The exit came from hard computer vision technology and a team Google wanted rather than from a revenue business.
notes: The dataset description describes a video dating app, which is a later or mixed up description; the 2012 company was webcam gesture control. Company site flutterapp.com returned HTTP 503 so was not read. Wikipedia reports 40M as the price; TechCrunch says terms undisclosed and 40M unconfirmed, so no amount is recorded. Seed investors per TechCrunch also include angels. Founders' education and prior employers not found in opened sources. Competitor dates are 2012-04 and not an exhaustive list; Leap Motion not found in sources dated near the batch.
